title: Add athena land --pr for owned mode with a gh REST host client
summary: Builds the command slice that D86 deferred. `athena land --pr <job>` pushes the job's work branch through the existing `check_push` guard, opens a PR, waits for checks, merges, then runs `check_merged`. The host client shells out to `gh api` REST endpoints only, with no GraphQL, and sits behind the existing `Host` trait plus new traits so tests use fakes.

defaults_applied.how: The host client is Rust that runs the `gh` binary; no scripts.
Reuse the installed `gh` instead of building an HTTP client or adding a GitHub crate, and record the call in decisions.md.
The new module has fake-backed unit tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
REST-only is enforced by a test that checks every `gh api` call path, not only by prose.
Owned mode only; stealth is left to a later slice.
The decision entry and the design update are written for an outside reader.
Behavior criteria are limited to cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.

assumptions: Owned mode only; stealth mode (neutral branch name, stripped body) stays a later slice.

The host is GitHub, reached by running `gh api` as a subprocess. The client uses REST routes only: POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls, GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}, GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/check-runs and /status, PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge. It never calls `gh pr` subcommands or `gh api graphql`.
'Wait for checks' polls the check status with a bounded timeout and interval. It merges only when every check has passed, and stops with a clear message on failure or timeout.
The push is a regular `git push` with no force flag, run only after `check_push` allows it. The remote head is read with `git ls-remote` or from the REST API.
The PR link is stored with `store_link` before the merge, and the link file is kept until the merge is observed (D86 tradeoff). The outcome is applied with `apply_outcome`.
The PR body is generated from the job's request, criteria, findings and job id, as design section 5.1 step 3 says.
Exit codes follow the CLI convention: 0 when landed and verified, 2 when not landed (checks failed, merged-unverified), 1 when Athena itself erred.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new host-client module in crates/athena-core implements the `Host` trait (and any new traits for opening a PR, reading check status and merging) by running `gh api` with REST paths only. No source file contains a GraphQL query or `gh api graphql`, and no `gh pr` subcommand is used.
The CLI has a `land` subcommand with a `--pr` flag that takes a job id and an optional `--json`. It is wired in crates/athena-cli, and `athena land --help` documents it.

The flow is push, open, wait for checks, merge, then the merged-content check. The push goes through `check_push` first and has no force option. The PR link is stored via `store_link`, the outcome goes through `apply_outcome`, and the link survives `clean_job` until the merge is observed.

Unit tests with a fake `gh` runner or fake host cover the happy path (landed), failed checks (no merge), a check timeout, a refused non-fast-forward push, and a merge that is not the verified content (merged-unverified). They also assert that every recorded `gh api` call uses a REST path and never graphql. Run `cargo test` and confirm they pass.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` and confirm both are clean. Run `cargo test` for the whole workspace and confirm it passes, including the existing pr.rs tests.

docs/decisions.md gets a new decision entry for this slice. It records the buy-first call (shelling out to gh versus an HTTP crate) and the REST-only choice, and docs/design/native-pr-landing.md is updated to say the command is built. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry.

out_of_scope: Stealth mode (neutral branch names, stripped PR body, leak checks).
Auto-merge settings, forks, or any host other than GitHub.
Changing the records schema, the gate, or the existing push guard and merged-content logic beyond what wiring needs.
Rebasing or re-verifying stale or merged-unverified jobs.
Running against the live GitHub API in tests.
departures: This is a multi-file feature with a CLI command, a subprocess client, a polling loop, tests and docs. It is larger than the typical historical job, so cost and time sit well above the reference. Pass probability is lower because the flow has many branches and the verifier can run only cargo commands.
